topic: How do GEO versus LEO satellite orbits impact power flux density and resolution trade-offs in passive radar systems using Inmarsat and Iridium?
consensus_response: The choice of satellite signal between Inmarsat (GEO) and Iridium (LEO) significantly impacts the power flux density and resolution in passive radar systems. Inmarsat's higher altitude leads to higher power flux density due to increased gain, but its narrower beamwidth reduces coverage. Iridium's lower altitude offers a wider beamwidth and potentially better coverage but with lower power flux density. Advanced signal processing techniques can be used to mitigate the trade-offs and optimize the performance of the system. However, the effectiveness of these techniques depends on the specific requirements of the system and the characteristics of the satellite signal. The choice of satellite signal will depend on the specific requirements of the passive radar system, including the desired resolution, coverage, and interference tolerance.
